objective: A single guided scientific manual with a compact exact public API reference.
principles: Preserve verified knowledge, not legacy pages.
Organize authored content around reader intent and scientific workflow.
Give each normal user task and concept one canonical narrative home.
Integrate focused procedures and contextual troubleshooting into workflow chapters.
Use runtime introspection for exact signatures and a user-facing manifest for explanations.
Keep implementation, persistence, qualification, and repository-maintenance detail outside MkDocs.

reader_modes.learn: Follow a tested progression from first interface to interpreted calculator-backed results.
reader_modes.use: Complete one stage of a real CALM study and make the required scientific decisions.
reader_modes.understand: Interpret the mathematics, assumptions, and limitations behind CALM inputs and outputs.
reader_modes.reference: Look up exact API behavior, conventions, support boundaries, or a user-visible symptom.

navigation.label: Home
navigation.purpose: Orient prospective and current users around CALM’s coherent-interface workflow, shortest successful path, principal outputs, and scientific limits.

navigation.label: Install
navigation.purpose: Define the supported source-checkout installation paths, dependency profiles, environment validation steps, and the boundary between geometry-only and calculator-backed workflows.

children.label: Build your first interface
children.purpose: This calculator-free tutorial will take a new user from packaged tutorial structures to one saved, constructed, and unrelaxed coherent interface.

children.label: Compare candidates
children.purpose: This tutorial will teach users to inspect candidate tables, interpret the strain–size tradeoff, use Pareto filtering, and choose candidates for an explicit modeling objective.

children.label: Refine, relax, and evaluate
children.purpose: This calculator-backed tutorial will teach strain allocation, registry refinement, relaxation inspection, raw energies, and one explicit thermodynamic reference convention.

children.label: Projects
children.purpose: This chapter will explain how users create, reopen, inspect, trace, export, reproduce, and recover incompatible CALM studies without exposing storage schemas or persistence implementation.

children.label: Materials
children.purpose: This chapter will explain supported structure inputs, material preparation, periodicity, calculator association, inspection, and export.

children.label: Surfaces and terminations
children.purpose: This chapter will explain orientation, finite slabs, vacuum, thickness, generated alternatives, explicit termination selection, and contact-face interpretation.

children.label: Searches and candidates
children.purpose: This chapter will explain bounded coherent matching, search limits, candidate inspection, strain and size interpretation, Pareto filtering, selection, and no-candidate recovery.

children.label: Build and refine interfaces
children.purpose: This chapter will explain candidate construction, gap and vacuum choices, strain partitioning, registry refinement, multi-candidate workflows, inspection, and export.

children.label: Relax and evaluate
children.purpose: This chapter will explain calculator requirements, relaxation settings, convergence inspection, raw energies, reference structures, derived quantities, and scientific limitations.

children.label: Datasets and campaigns
children.purpose: This optional advanced chapter will explain eligibility, features, targets, grouping, leakage prevention, splitting, export, campaign cases, and comparison.

children.label: Surface models
children.purpose: This chapter will connect crystallographic orientation to periodic surface cells, finite slabs, explicit terminations, and the limitations of unreconstructed finite models.

children.label: Surface cells and supercells
children.purpose: This chapter will explain lattice bases, equivalent representations, bounded supercells, and the growth of area and atom count without reconstructing implementation canonicalization.

children.label: Coherent matching, strain, and Pareto selection
children.purpose: This chapter will explain common periodic cells, deformation maps, principal strain, area and shape mismatch, and the strain–size tradeoff used to interpret candidates.

children.label: Strain partitioning and registry
children.purpose: This chapter will explain how coherent mismatch is shared, how periodic in-plane translations define registry, and when refinement requires a calculator.

children.label: Relaxation, energy, and reference conventions
children.purpose: This chapter will explain local relaxation, convergence versus stability, raw total energies, normalization, explicit reference cycles, and derived interfacial quantities.

children.label: Public API
children.purpose: This page will explain CALM’s single supported namespace and route readers to exact generated signatures for project operations, inputs, settings, returned objects, tables, exceptions, and utilities.

children.label: Project operations
children.purpose: Exact signatures for supported Project operations, grouped by workflow role.

children.label: Inputs and settings
children.purpose: Exact constructors and fields for supported user-authored inputs and settings.

children.label: Returned objects and tables
children.purpose: Curated user-relevant returned-object members and supported table views.

children.label: Exceptions and utilities
children.purpose: Exact public exceptions and file or serialization utilities.

children.label: Units and conventions
children.purpose: This page will provide the canonical units, coordinate conventions, basis-vector convention, strain convention, periodic directions, and normalization rules used across CALM.

children.label: Terminology
children.purpose: This page will define the compact user vocabulary used throughout the manual and distinguish names, identifiers, searches, candidates, interfaces, results, datasets, and campaigns.

children.label: Supported scope
children.purpose: This page will state what CALM constructs or evaluates, what it does not infer, and which assumptions limit scientific interpretation.

children.label: Calculator support
children.purpose: This page will distinguish registered providers, dependency availability, model compatibility, scientific suitability, and the reference data required for derived quantities.

children.label: Geometry and project troubleshooting
children.purpose: This symptom index will route users to contextual remedies for structure input, surface generation, candidate search, interface construction, project lookup, and project compatibility problems.

children.label: Calculation and data troubleshooting
children.purpose: This symptom index will route users to contextual remedies for calculator availability, relaxation, energies, references, datasets, exports, and campaigns.

tutorial_product.geometry_system: Packaged LiF/Li2O tutorial structures for the calculator-free first and candidate-comparison tutorials.

calculator_tutorial.decision: Use the registered ASE provider with EMT and an EMT-compatible Cu/Ni demonstration system.
calculator_tutorial.interpretation_boundary: The example demonstrates CALM workflow mechanics and reference bookkeeping; it is not evidence that EMT is accurate for a user’s target interface.

tutorial_product.notebooks: Optional notebooks are generated from tested canonical tutorial sources; handwritten parallel notebooks are prohibited.

legacy_replacement.redirect_policy: No compatibility redirects are created unless a published legacy URL is later shown to require one.
